# Inference on single proportion

$p$ = proportion of prosocial choices Chimp A makes when it has a partner

$X \sim Binom(90, p)$

satisfies almost all the assumptions (mostly will violate S assiumption)

```{r}
x = 60 # number of prosocial choices
n = 90 # no. of trials
p_hat = x/n # p.e
se_w = sqrt(p_hat*(1-p_hat)/n) # Wald adjusted standard error

# 99% CI for p

z = qnorm(0.995) # cv with c+(1-c)/2
z

p_hat + c(-1, 1)*z*se_w
```


$$H_0: p = 0.5, H_{\alpha}: p > 0.5$$

```{r}
alpha = 0.01
z = (p_hat-0.5)/se_w # test statitics
z

p_val = pnorm(z, lower.tail = F)
p_val

# p-val < alpha, we reject H_0, which implies that there is sufficient to support the claim that Chimp A is making prosocial choices
```

# Diff of prop

$p_1 = $ Prob of making prosocial choices when Chimp A has no partner (true p1 should be 0.5 or random choice)

$p_2 = $ Prob of making prosocial choices when Chimp A has a partner (true p2 should be more than 0.5 or prosocial choice)

parameter: $p_1-p_2$
p.e: $\hat{p}_1 - \hat{p}_2$
s.e adj: CI: $$se_{adj} = \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}_1(1-\hat{p}_1)}{n_1}+\frac{\hat{p}_2(1-\hat{p}_2)}{n_2}}$$


hypo test: $$se_{adj} = \sqrt{\frac{\tilde{p}(1-\tilde{p})}{n_1}+\frac{\tilde{p}(1-\tilde{p})}{n_2}}$$

$$H_0: p_1-p_2 = 0 \\ H_{\alpha}: p_1-p_2 < 0$$



```{r}
x1 = 16
n1 = 30
x2 = 60 
n2 = 90

phat1 = x1/n1
phat2 = x2/n2
ptilde = (x1+x2)/(n1+n2) # global prop

cv = qnorm(0.975)

se_ci = sqrt((phat1*(1-phat1)/n1)+(phat2*(1-phat2)/n2)) # se for CI


# 95% CI for p1-p2
(phat1-phat2) + c(-1,1)*cv*se_ci # note that the CI includes 0, which means that monkey makes prosocial choices irrespective of the presence of a partner


se_ht = sqrt((ptilde*(1-ptilde)*(1/n1+ 1/n2))) # se for hypothesis testing
             
z = (phat1-phat2)/se_ht # test statistic

pnorm(z) # p-val and comparing it with alpha = 0.05, we fail to reject H_0, whihc also coincides with the 95% CI built earlier
```
